BookCreate.description: Add a book the reader never found. Lands as ``manual`` with one copy.
BookCreate.title: BookCreate

BookDTO.description:
A book and its copies.

Copies are embedded in the LIST response, not fetched per row. With one
copy per book on the real data that is roughly a 2x payload, and the
alternative — the book surface firing a request per card (UI_PLAN §5) —
is far worse. Revisit if a library ever has many multi-copy books.

author_key.description: Normalized author, the key the author chip groups on (§5.1 — authors are strings, not entities).
author_key.title: Author Key

status.description: auto | approved | manual — the strongest claim among this book's copies.
status.title: Status

BookDTO.title: BookDTO

BookPageDTO.description:
One page plus the total, so the client can render "1-20 of 251"
without a second round trip.
BookPageDTO.title: BookPageDTO

BookPatch.description:
Fix a title or an author by hand. Either field, or both.

Saving marks the book ``manual`` — a human decision outranking an auto one
(UI_PLAN §5). That is applied by the domain, not here.
BookPatch.title: BookPatch

BookSort.description:
Sort orders §6 lists as "Must". ``TITLE``/``AUTHOR`` sort by NORMALIZED
forms, so Hebrew orders sensibly regardless of nikud, geresh or a leading
particle in the stored string.

``AUTHOR`` orders by SURNAME (``app.domain.text.author_sort_key``), the way
a shelf is filed — not by the stored string, which would put every author
under their given name. Every implementation must agree; the contract
suite asserts it against each one.
BookSort.title: BookSort

CaptureBinding.description:
What :meth:`create` produced — the photo AND the shelf it landed on.

Both, never just the capture: when the shelf was auto-created the client
has no other way to learn its id, and a second round trip to discover the
thing you just implicitly made is the sort of gap that gets papered over
with a client-side guess. Same reasoning as the copy routes returning the
whole ``BookDTO``.

shelf_created.description: True when no shelf_id was given and one was made.
shelf_created.title: Shelf Created

CaptureBinding.title: CaptureBinding

CaptureCreate.description:
File a photo.

``shelf_id`` is optional and that is the point of P2.2: a photo that names
no shelf gets a fresh unnamed one, because a capture with no shelf is a
read with nothing to reconcile against (§5.6). *"Unassigned"* on screen
means *not yet named*, never *not yet filed*.

order.description: Omit to append after the last photo at this shelf+depth.
order.title: Order

CaptureCreate.title: CaptureCreate

CaptureDTO.description: One photo of part of a shelf, keyed by ``(shelf, depth, order)``.

image_id.description: Reference, never bytes — blobs live behind BlobStore (P3.5). Also what identifies an unnamed shelf on screen.
image_id.title: Image Id

order.description: Position among this shelf+depth's photos, left-to-right or right-to-left per the shelf's reading direction.
order.title: Order

CaptureDTO.title: CaptureDTO

CapturePatch.description:
Re-bind a photo: move it to another shelf, another row, or another
position. This is the inline assignment the intake UI performs.
CapturePatch.title: CapturePatch

CopyCreate.description:
*"I have another copy"* (§5.1) — the only path that creates a second
physical object. No ``shelf_id`` here: shelves don't exist until P2.1, so
every copy today is unlocated regardless of how it was created.
CopyCreate.title: CopyCreate

CopyDTO.description: One physical object. Created only by a human action (§5.1).

depth.description: Row front-to-back. A located copy always has one; an unlocated copy has neither shelf nor depth (§5.7).
depth.title: Depth

last_seen.description: Most recent provenance entry, if any.

sighting_count.description: Length of the provenance list; the list itself is on the book detail, not in every row.
sighting_count.title: Sighting Count

CopyDTO.title: CopyDTO

CopyPatch.description:
Fix a copy's own label/tags/condition. Object-level, unlike
:class:`BookPatch` — describing "paperback, torn cover" is not a claim
about the book's identity, so unlike a title/author edit this does not
change the copy's status.
CopyPatch.title: CopyPatch

LendRequest.description:
*"Lend it out"*. ``lent_at`` is server time (the ``Clock``, like
``added_at``), never client-supplied — a borrow date is a fact about when
the server recorded the action, not something the caller should be able
to backdate.
LendRequest.title: LendRequest

LendingDTO.description: Per copy, never per book — you lend an object, not a work.
LendingDTO.title: LendingDTO

LibraryRefDTO.description:
The tenant reference the client echoes back on every request.

Present from the very first endpoint on purpose: the client is
tenant-aware from P1.0 (§1.3), even though there is exactly one library
until pillar 3.
LibraryRefDTO.title: LibraryRefDTO

MetaResponse.description: Service identity + the caller's resolved library.
MetaResponse.title: MetaResponse

ShelfCreate.description: Declare a shelf. Every field optional — see :class:`ShelfDTO.label`.
ShelfCreate.title: ShelfCreate

ShelfDTO.description: A shelf's identity. No address — that is pillar 6 (plan §1.1).

capture_count.description: Photos filed against this shelf, across every depth.
capture_count.title: Capture Count

depth_count.description: Rows front-to-back, declared by the owner — never detected (§5.7). 1 unless a row behind was added.
depth_count.title: Depth Count

label.description: Optional. Empty is normal: identity is free, so a shelf is never required to be named. An unnamed one is shown by the image it came from.
label.title: Label

virtual.description: The wishlist. Excluded from shelf listings by default.
virtual.title: Virtual

ShelfDTO.title: ShelfDTO

ShelfPatch.description:
Name a shelf, or clear the name. ``depth_count`` is deliberately NOT
here: adding a row behind is its own endpoint, because §5.7 makes it an
explicit declaration rather than a number to nudge.
ShelfPatch.title: ShelfPatch

SightingDTO.description: One entry of a copy's append-only provenance (§5.2).

depth.description: Which row front-to-back (§5.7). Travels WITH shelf_id — both null or both set.
depth.title: Depth

shelf_id.description: Where this sighting happened. Null for the 251 imported books, whose recorded evidence is only run+spine.
shelf_id.title: Shelf Id

SightingDTO.title: SightingDTO

WorkFieldsDTO.description: Book-level user fields. You don't rate your second copy differently.
WorkFieldsDTO.title: WorkFieldsDTO

get.description:
One endpoint, two modes.

Searching is not a filter on top of a sort — relevance IS the order, so a
`sort` passed alongside `q` would be a promise the server cannot keep.
It is ignored rather than rejected: a UI that keeps a sort control on
screen while the user types should not start returning 400s mid-keystroke.

parameters.description: Hebrew search over title and author. When present the results are ordered by RELEVANCE and `sort`/`ascending` are ignored — the order is the answer.
parameters.name: q

A book the reader never found. Lands as ``manual`` — a person typed it,

get.description:
The honest answer to lock-in (§6): everything, in one file, always.

CSV is written with a UTF-8 BOM. Without it Excel opens a Hebrew CSV as
mojibake, and "my export is broken" is indistinguishable from "your data
is broken".
get.summary: Export the whole library (CSV or JSON)

delete.description:
*Delete from the library* — the destructive one of UI_PLAN §5's two
actions. *Remove from shelf* is a different thing entirely and does not
live here; it changes a copy, it does not remove a record.

patch.description:
Editing marks the book ``manual`` (UI_PLAN §5). The domain applies
that; this route only decides what an unresolvable rename returns.

Object-level metadata, not identity — unlike :func:`patch_book` this
never changes the copy's status (`app.domain.book.edit_copy`).
patch.summary: Fix a copy's label, tags or condition

post.description:
409 if the copy is already out — return it first (§5.2: one borrower
per copy, or the earlier one is silently lost from "who has my books").

409 if the copy was never lent, or already marked returned — there is
no open loan to close (`app.domain.book.return_copy`).

File a photo — with a shelf if one is named, on a fresh one if not.

Returns BOTH the capture and its shelf: when the shelf was auto-created the
client has no other way to learn its id, and a second round trip to
discover the thing you just implicitly made is what gets papered over with
a client-side guess.

patch.description:
Move a photo to another shelf, another row, or another position.

This is the inline assignment the intake UI performs. Moving to a shelf
that is not one row deeper than the caller thinks is a **409** naming the
declared depth, not a silent clamp: filing a photo at a row that does not
exist would give reconciliation a location with no counterpart in the room.

get.description:
Every shelf, named ones first and alphabetically, then unnamed ones
oldest-first. Not paged — a personal library has tens of shelves.

parameters.description: Include the wishlist. Excluded by default: it holds books the owner does not own, so counting it inflates both the shelf list and the apparent size of the library.
parameters.name: include_virtual

schema.description: Include the wishlist. Excluded by default: it holds books the owner does not own, so counting it inflates both the shelf list and the apparent size of the library.
schema.title: Include Virtual
Response List Shelves Api V1 Shelves Get

post.description:
Declare a shelf up front. Every field is optional (identity is free).

Depth is not settable here on purpose — a shelf starts one row deep and
gains rows through :func:`add_a_row_behind`, because §5.7 makes the second
row a declaration rather than a number to guess at during creation.

delete.description:
Remove a shelf that holds no photos. **409** if it does.

Not a cascade: its captures are the record a re-read diffs against (§5.6).
This is for the shelf created by mistake, not for clearing one out.

patch.description:
Name a shelf, or clear the name — ``""`` is a legal value, not a
missing one, because a label the owner no longer wants should not be kept
just to avoid an empty string.

parameters.description: Narrow to one row front-to-back. §5.6's not-seen rule and the diff view are per depth, and §5.7 #2 forbids merging overlaps across depths.
parameters.name: depth

schema.description: Narrow to one row front-to-back. §5.6's not-seen rule and the diff view are per depth, and §5.7 #2 forbids merging overlaps across depths.
schema.title: Depth
Response List Shelf Captures Api V1 Shelves  Shelf Id  Captures Get

post.description:
*"Add a row behind this one"* (§5.7) — the declaration that cannot be
detected, because nothing in a photo says "this is the row behind"; the
front books are simply absent.

Its own endpoint rather than a ``depth_count`` field so the client cannot
set it to 5 in one step and leave three rows nobody photographed. Refused
on the wishlist, which has no behind.
